Classical graph embedding methods (e.g., spectral methods such as Laplacian Eigenmaps or IsoMap) are usually limited by needing the whole graph up front and by costly eigen-decompositions that scale poorly with the number of vertices, which makes them hard to apply to large or evolving networks. DeepWalk can still build a Hierarchical Softmax tree without seeing the entire graph when the vertex frequencies in its short random walks follow a power-law (scale-free) distribution. In that case the Huffman-coded tree can be built from the observed frequencies, which is what allows the approach to work online and at scale.
